judgment.observations: The reconstruction preserves the recognizable electronics workbench layout, including monitor, instruments, keyboard, meters, lamp, drawer organizers and tangled leads. Framing is more frontal and the desk appears cleaner and brighter. The monitor is smaller and more upright; the oscilloscope and keyboard have simplified shapes and controls. The reference's dense cable clutter, wall pliers, equipment details and right-side supplies are substantially reduced or omitted. Drawer organizers are pale rather than dark, the desktop is lighter, and most surfaces look matte and uniform instead of worn, reflective or textured. The lamp has a simpler rectangular silhouette, and the soldering area and tool case differ noticeably in shape and placement. These differences produce moderate overall similarity despite a strong match in broad object categories.
judgment.uncertain_3d_hypotheses: The rendered keyboard, instruments and meters appear to rest on the desktop, but exact contact and support cannot be established from this view. Some leads appear unusually flat or loosely connected to equipment; this may reflect simplified routing or image visibility. The lamp support and right-side soldering assembly appear spatially different from the reference, although perspective and occlusion make their depth relationships uncertain.
